name: Abraham Vereide

summary.text: Abraham Vereide, a Methodist minister, built the prayer-group movement (International Christian Leadership, later known as the Fellowship or the Family) that held its dedicatory breakfast with President Eisenhower at Washington's Mayflower Hotel on February 5, 1953 — the first Presidential (now National) Prayer Breakfast. Senator Frank Carlson's prayer group and Billy Graham persuaded Eisenhower to attend.

sources.title: National Prayer Breakfast: What Does Its History Reveal?

facts.claim: Eisenhower attended the dedicatory breakfast of International Christian Leadership on February 5, 1953, about two weeks after his inauguration, at the Mayflower Hotel; the movement was Vereide's and continues under the names the Family or the Fellowship.
facts.quote: Eisenhower attended the dedicatory breakfast of the International Christian Leadership on Feb. 5, 1953

facts.claim: Senator Frank Carlson suggested Eisenhower meet his prayer group, and Billy Graham persuaded Eisenhower to attend after he initially declined.
